The primary-source packet supports the core lifetime distinction: alloca-style stack-frame storage is tied to the caller frame and released when the call returns, while malloc-style dynamic storage has an independently managed lifetime until released. The candidate makes this lifetime/management distinction the organizing principle rather than relying on size or speed mnemonics.

The JVM-specific sections are correctly bounded. JVMS 26 specifies a private JVM stack per thread, a shared JVM heap, frame push/pop behavior, StackOverflowError, managed heap reclamation, and implementation freedom around layout; the candidate uses these as runtime examples instead of promoting them to universal language-independent guarantees.
